title: The Race of the Rising Beam
story: Skerrywake the Fog Lurker smothers the lighthouse beam so ships wreck on the rocks. Mr 6 discovers the beacon lamp burns oil at 0.6 liters per hour, and the reservoir holds 21 liters. A ship is nine hours out at sea, but the fog will only lift when the lamp has burned every drop.
question: How many hours can the lamp burn on 21 liters at 0.6 liters per hour?
hint: Ask yourself: how many groups of 0.6 fit inside 21? Dividing by 0.6 is the same as dividing by 6 and then multiplying by 10.
victory: Mr 6 announced thirty-five hours and Skerrywake groaned — the fog can only hold its breath for thirty. The lurker wisped away, and the ship sailed in on a beam bright as a promise.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight atop a storm-lashed lighthouse gallery holding a sword aloft as a swirling fog creature recoils from a widening golden beam over a dark sea.
solution: Ask how many groups of 0.6 liters fit into 21 liters: 21 ÷ 0.6.
Divide by 6 and then multiply by 10: 21 ÷ 6 = 3.5, and 3.5 × 10 = 35.
The lamp can burn for 35 hours.
praise: You spotted that this was a division — dividing by a decimal like 0.6 just needs that ×10 trick to finish.
